Hi all — draft answers below, and I've attached the runbook + RTO/RPO matrix. Kept it concise as requested; happy to expand any item.

1) RTO / RPO (hosted API):
- Typical RTO (regional outage, automatic routing to healthy region): 10–20 minutes for control-plane DNS and routing convergence; 20–45 minutes to reach pre-failure latency percentiles once caches warm.
- Worst-case RTO (large model families cold-starts / model rehydration): up to 3 hours for cold model load in a region without pre-warmed artifacts.
- RPO: customer metadata and config are replicated across regions with sub-minute propagation for control-plane state (near-zero RPO for configuration). For in-flight inference requests and ephemeral session state, RPO is best-effort — in-flight tokens are not replayed; we treat those as potential loss and recommend idempotent client-side retry.

2) Multi-region failover model:
- Primary model: active-active for stateless request routing at the API layer (traffic can be balanced across regions).
- Control-plane and leader election: active-passive for certain stateful control-plane components with automatic failover via consensus (etcd/raft).
- Failover triggers: automated health checks with policy-driven routing (latency/circuit-breaker) and manual override via the Console. Cross-region failover is automated for traffic routing; customers can pin regions for Dedicated workloads.

3) Replication of artifacts, caches, data:
- Model artifacts: proactively replicated to target regions based on policy. For hosted catalog models we maintain pre-seeded artifact stores in each supported region; for large custom models we provide async replication with pre-warm options.
- KV caches: best-effort warm-cache strategies — we replicate cache metadata and hot prefixes to adjacent regions; full KV cache state is not synchronously replicated due to size and throughput considerations.
- Customer data: customer-controlled persistent data (logs, telemetry) is stored in object storage with cross-region replication (CRR) enabled; control-plane metadata stored in our primary database with async replicas and write-forwarding to avoid split-brain.

4) Warm-standby and time-to-throughput:
- Dedicated (reserved) customers: optional warm-standby pools can be configured (pre-provisioned GPUs with preloaded model weights). Typical failover to full throughput for pre-warmed pools: 5–15 minutes.
- Hosted (multi-tenant): we maintain a pool of pre-warmed instances for top-weighted models; for non-prewarmed model families, region rehydration can take 45–180 minutes depending on model size (weights I/O bound).

5) Testing cadence and evidence:
- Quarterly tabletop failover drills and annual full-region failover exercises (last full exercise: 2025-11-17).
- Runbooks and drill notes available: see attached RedwooD_DR_Runbook_v1.2.pdf and RTO/RPO matrix. We also provide summarized test reports for enterprise customers on request.

Known limitations / expected data loss scenarios:
- In-flight inference tokens and ephemeral session data may be lost across abrupt failovers; clients should implement idempotency and request-level retries.
- For very large custom models without pre-warm agreements, cold-start rehydration increases RTO significantly.

Attachments: Redwood_DR_Runbook_v1.2.pdf; Redwood_RTO_RPO_Matrix_2026.xlsx; warm-standby-architecture-diagram.png

Marissa

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Please see our numbered responses below and the attached artifacts (runbook and RTO/RPO matrix) for more detail. Short answers are provided first with a one-line pointer to where we document evidence.

1) RTO / RPO (summary):
- Hosted API typical RTO: ~10–20 minutes for routing; 20–45 minutes to fully warm caches. Worst-case (cold rehydration for very large models): up to 3 hours.
- Dedicated (reserved pools) RTO: 5–15 minutes when warm-standby is enabled; 30–90 minutes if new model weights must be loaded.
- RPO: control-plane metadata — near-zero (sub-minute replication). In-flight requests — best-effort; recommend idempotent client retries. Evidence: Redwood_RTO_RPO_Matrix_2026.xlsx (attached) and last full-region test 2025-11-17 (see runbook).

2) Multi-region failover model:
- API traffic: active-active routing with policy-driven automatic failover; control-plane: active-passive with consensus-based leader election. Customers may pin Dedicated capacity to a region; cross-region failover for Dedicated requires configured warm-standby. Documentation: DR runbook (attached).

3) Replication approach:
- Model artifacts: pre-seeded for hosted catalog models; async replication for custom uploads with pre-warm option.
- Caches: hot-prefix replication; full caches are not synchronously mirrored.
- Persistent customer artefacts: object storage with CRR; control-plane DB uses async replicas with automated failover.

4) Warm-standby options & throughput:
- Dedicated customers: warm-standby pools available as an add-on (5–15 min to full throughput).
- Hosted: we pre-warm common model families; non-prewarmed large models may take 45–180 minutes.

5) Testing cadence & evidence:
- Quarterly drills, annual full failovers. Last full test: 2025-11-17; summary and logs in runbook. We can provide redacted drill reports under NDA.

Limitations / recommended mitigations:
- Expect possible loss of ephemeral in-flight state during abrupt region cutovers — build idempotency and client retry logic.
- For strict RTO/RPO SLAs we recommend Dedicated + warm-standby configuration.

Attached: Redwood_DR_Runbook_v1.2.pdf; Redwood_RTO_RPO_Matrix_2026.xlsx; warm-standby-architecture-diagram.png

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute technical walk-through next week to step through the runbook and the warm-standby options.

Regards,
Jonas Weber
VP, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
